scenes.title: Deep time, one diorama
scenes.copy: Restage the Mesozoic by era. Context is earth history. Evidence is named taxa and published sizes.
scenes.narration: Welcome to Dinosaur Hall. This is a deep-time field guide — a Three.js diorama you can restage by era, plus a museum wall of named species. Context versus Evidence stays on the label.

scenes.title: First footsteps
scenes.copy: 252 to 201 million years ago — early bipedal hunters and long-necked precursors.
scenes.narration: Chapter one — the Triassic. After the end-Permian collapse, the first dinosaurs appear. Coelophysis and Plateosaurus remind us early forms were not all movie giants.

scenes.title: Fern forests and titans
scenes.copy: Sauropods, Stegosaurus, Allosaurus — the classic Morrison fauna.
scenes.narration: Chapter two — the Jurassic. Fern greens, pillar-legged sauropods, plate-backed Stegosaurus, and Allosaurus on the hunt. T. rex is still eighty million years away.

scenes.title: Horns, crests, and impact dusk
scenes.copy: Tyrannosaurs, ceratopsians, hadrosaurs — then the end-Cretaceous winter.
scenes.narration: Chapter three — the Cretaceous. Flowering plants spread. Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops, and crested hadrosaurs fill the hall until the impact winter closes the era.

scenes.title: Pterosaurs and mosasaurs
scenes.copy: Flying and swimming Mesozoic reptiles sit outside Dinosauria — labeled clearly here.
scenes.narration: One sharp scholarly hook: not everything Mesozoic is a dinosaur. Pteranodon is a pterosaur. Mosasaurus is a marine lizard. We keep those labels honest.

scenes.title: True-to-scale lengths
scenes.copy: Pick two animals. Numbers come from the field guide — not movie posters.
scenes.narration: Use the size compare. A human silhouette anchors the diorama. Velociraptor was turkey-sized. Diplodocus stretched toward twenty-seven meters.

scenes.title: Check the evidence
scenes.copy: Five quick questions — eras, non-dinosaurs, and movie myths.
scenes.narration: Finish with the field quiz. If Allosaurus shared the Jurassic with Stegosaurus, you already know more than the movies.
